assumptions: The assessed event is an actual STR submission by an entity within the circular's licensed-firm categories.
The event timestamp is after the stated STREAMS 2 launch boundary, with the applicable timezone and boundary interpretation established separately.
The event used one and only one of the three listed STREAMS 2 submission methods.

citations.quote: With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.

children.distinction: This child formalizes the channel, timing and method alternatives. It does not decide the separate footnote 3 e-Cert requirement for XML or PDF submissions.

facts.meaning: The reporting entity is within the circular's licensed-firm categories.
facts.name: licensed_firm

facts.meaning: The assessed STR submission event occurred at or after the STREAMS 2 effective launch boundary.
facts.name: post_launch_submission

facts.meaning: The event used STREAMS 2 as its submission channel.
facts.name: used_streams2

facts.meaning: The event uploaded a completed STR in the prescribed PDF format.
facts.name: used_completed_prescribed_pdf

facts.meaning: The event completed the STREAMS 2 web-based STR form.
facts.name: used_web_form

formalization.result: (and licensed_firm post_launch_submission used_streams2 (or used_xml used_completed_prescribed_pdf used_web_form))

questions: What evidence establishes the submitting entity's classification within the circular's licensed-firm categories?
What is the assessed event's timestamp, and which timezone governs the stated launch boundary?
Was this an actual STR submission to the JFIU, and which listed method did this event use?
children.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] For the selected event, the channel-and-method component is satisfied only if the submitting entity is an in-scope licensed firm, the event is post-launch, the event used STREAMS 2, and exactly one listed method was used: XML, completed prescribed PDF upload, or web form completion.
children.subject: STREAMS 2 channel, launch boundary and listed submission method

assumptions: The XML or prescribed-PDF branch is selected for the event.
The source statement that a Hongkong Post e-Cert is required applies to the selected submission.
No conclusion is drawn from certificate availability alone.
The operational act, certificate-holder identity, authorization, validity and authentication conditions are not inferred.

citations.quote: submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.

children.distinction: The retained authorities establish a submission-related e-Cert requirement but do not define the operational relationship that makes the requirement satisfied. A complete Boolean compliance formula therefore requires additional authoritative instructions or event evidence.
questions: For this XML or PDF event, what operational relationship between a Hongkong Post e-Cert and the submission satisfies footnote 3?
Does the applicable technical material impose certificate-holder, authorization, signing, attachment, authentication or validity conditions?
What evidence establishes that the required relationship occurred for this event?
children.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] The XML or prescribed-PDF branch is compliant only when the submission-related Hongkong Post e-Cert requirement is satisfied in the manner required by the applicable JFIU instructions. The retained authorities do not specify that manner, so this component remains unresolved pending authoritative technical or procedural material.
children.subject: Operational meaning of the footnote 3 Hongkong Post e-Cert requirement

obligations.explanation: The parent compliance question is decomposed into a formalizable channel/method component and an unresolved certificate component. The children together restate the parent's selected-event relation; the certificate child remains unresolved and cannot be settled by the first child.
The licensed-firm classification remains an explicit judgment-bearing fact in the channel/method child.
The launch and resumption provisions remain an explicit post-launch condition; no timezone or boundary interpretation is invented.
The event classification as an actual STR submission and its method remain explicit questions and facts.
The single-method-per-event condition is retained in the channel/method decomposition.
The XML/PDF footnote marker remains attached to the certificate child; no requirement is inferred for the web form.
The unresolved availability-versus-operational-use issue is preserved as the certificate child and remains unresolved.
Certificate-holder, authorization, attachment and validity mechanics remain expressly unresolved.
The selected scope continues to exclude XML-schema conformity, technical testing, substantive STR adequacy and overall legal compliance.
The entity classification question is represented by the licensed_firm fact and retained as judgment-bearing.
The event timestamp and governing timezone remain required to establish post_launch_submission.
The actual submission event, channel and method are represented in the first child.
The prescribed-form, completion and upload conditions are represented by used_completed_prescribed_pdf.
The certificate relationship remains unresolved and requires authoritative material or event evidence.
Certificate-holder, authorization and validity conditions remain unresolved.
The separately provided XML schema and technical-test instructions remain outside this bounded decomposition and are not inferred.
The blackout urgent-contact instruction remains a separate event classification and is not folded into the post-launch channel formula.
The outside-channel resubmission obligation remains separate; no deadline or completion fact is invented.

value.parent_relation: The children partition the parent's selected post-launch compliance question into (i) channel, timing and listed-method conditions and (ii) the unresolved footnote 3 e-Cert condition. No child alone settles the parent when the selected XML or PDF branch requires the unresolved certificate component.
residual_questions: What authoritative JFIU material defines how a Hongkong Post e-Cert satisfies footnote 3 for XML and prescribed-PDF submissions?
What event evidence establishes the relevant certificate relationship, holder, authorization and validity conditions, if any?
What timezone and boundary convention govern the launch and blackout timestamps?
